summary: Elizabeth Lopatto argues that the Sam Bankman-Fried fraud trial, as the prosecution's case nears its end, has exposed both FTX's widespread scams and the damage done to his closest friends and family, who are entangled in the case. Testimony from Wang, Ellison, Singh, Yedidia and Sun shows the fraud escalating gradually, with Alameda Research given special privileges and customer money flowing to investments, political donations and Bankman-Fried himself. Expert Peter Easton's tracing of funds showed philanthropy was a tiny fraction of spending, undercutting Bankman-Fried's altruism claims, while the defense has struggled to discredit the witnesses.
one_line: Lopatto argues the FTX trial testimony reveals escalating fraud and the ruined lives of Sam Bankman-Fried's friends and family caught up in the case.
key_facts: Sam Bankman-Fried is charged with seven counts: two counts of wire fraud and five conspiracy charges.
Adam Yedidia, Bankman-Fried's college roommate, testified with immunity and resigned after realizing FTX had stolen customer funds; he had texted 'I love you Sam... I'm not going anywhere.'
Gary Wang, FTX and Alameda co-founder, testified about 'allow_negative' code, switched on in July 2019, which let only Alameda avoid liquidation by FTX's risk management.
Wang set Alameda up with a line of credit that ultimately reached $65 billion, not visible to auditors according to Ellison.
Nishad Singh said he backdated transactions in December 2021 to push FTX's revenue 'over the line' to $1 billion, and pleaded guilty to six charges.
Caroline Ellison testified she created seven phony balance sheets and that Bankman-Fried knew Alameda took customer funds and invested them against her advice.
Wang, Singh and Ellison are now felons, facing possible prison or house arrest, restitution and job restrictions.
Peter Easton, a Notre Dame accounting professor who also helped investigate Enron and WorldCom, traced the $11.3 billion liability known in June 2022.
Easton's trace showed $1.2 billion repaid Genesis, $413 million went to Bankman-Fried through Paper Bird, $192 million to insiders, and $228 million to real estate.
Donations to Guarding Against Pandemics plus FTX Foundation philanthropy totaled less than $40 million, a tenth of what went to Paper Bird.
Singh testified to more than a billion dollars spent on celebrity endorsements, even though the futures platform didn't operate in the US.
Former FTX lawyer Can Sun testified that Bankman-Fried asked him to devise justifications for missing funds for Apollo in November, and Sun quit the next day.
Bankman-Fried's December 1st, 2022 Good Morning America appearance, which blamed the margin loan program, was shown in court.
